page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused instance within the network-optimized family. It provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores running on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is paired with 96 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 260 MB L3 cache. The instance features dedicated CPU scheduling with simultaneous multithreading active, supplemented by Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) and AVX-512 vector extensions. Discrete GPUs are absent, and no local disk storage is bundled, requiring network-attached storage for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate solid compute and compression throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 2214.0, positioning it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, alongside a multi-core score of 17853.0. Vector performance is highlighted by top-decile Geekbench results in image processing at 18779.0 and text processing at 2859.0. PassMark tests produced a CPU mark of 60557.12 and an encryption score of 46586.25, both placing within the upper quartile. High data compression efficiency is demonstrated by single-threaded gzip throughput of 34.41 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 285.51 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reached 75.61 GB/sec, while CPU-based inference achieved 386.47 tokens per second on text generation using a 135M parameter language model.

The hardware specification prioritizes CPU throughput over memory capacity and local IOPS density. With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and zero local NVMe storage, workloads demanding large in-memory footprints or high-speed local disk caches require external architectural accommodation. However, for compute-heavy parallel tasks, the dedicated core architecture offers predictable compute efficiency. The instance is well matched for software compilation pipelines, continuous integration systems, high-throughput static web serving, vectorized transformations, and CPU-driven batch processing.
